title: Open Agent Rules rule document
description: An OAR rule: where it applies (anchor + selector), when it applies (when + flow), and what happens (effect, transform, on_fire). Normative specification: https://openagentrules.org/spec/1.0/. The document world is closed — any key this schema does not declare is rejected, except x- extensions ([OAR-DOC-26], [OAR-DOC-27]).

oar.description: Format marker and version, <major>.<minor>, each part a decimal integer with no leading zero. Its presence identifies the document as an OAR rule. An engine rejects an unsupported major and any minor greater than its own ([OAR-DOC-3]-[OAR-DOC-5]).

id.description: Stable rule identifier. Never reused for a rule with a different meaning ([OAR-DOC-6]). Not required to correspond to any storage location ([OAR-DOC-28]).

namespace.description: Publisher scope. Rule identity is the qualified identifier <namespace>/<id>; absent means the loading host's own scope ([OAR-DOC-7], [OAR-DOC-8]).

kind.description: Fixes evaluation order and nothing else. Evaluation runs schema, then policy, then invariant, then detector ([OAR-DOC-10], [OAR-EVAL-1], [OAR-EVAL-2]).

anchor.description: The lifecycle moment. A core anchor identifier resolves through the host's anchor profile map; any other value is a host-native anchor ([OAR-DOC-12], [OAR-PROF-4], [OAR-PROF-5]).

when.description: Condition in the language of Appendix A, type-checked against the declared fact environment at load. Absent means the condition is satisfied ([OAR-DOC-14], [OAR-FACT-4]).

flow.description: Ordered step names matched as a non-contiguous subsequence of the recent activity window ([OAR-DOC-15], [OAR-FACT-12]).

effect.description: What the engine does when the rule fires ([OAR-DOC-11]).

enforcement.description: enforce applies the effect; monitor evaluates and records only; off loads without evaluating. off is the supported way to disable a rule — an unsatisfiable condition is not ([OAR-DOC-16], [OAR-OPS-2]).

mandatory.description: A mandatory rule cannot be disabled, downgraded, or suppressed by a configuration document, a pack, or another rule ([OAR-DOC-17], [OAR-OPS-7], [OAR-EVAL-17]).

on_error.description: What happens when the rule cannot be evaluated: fail_closed blocks under its own identifier, fail_open records and continues, or a bare or qualified rule identifier blocks under that rule's identifiers instead ([OAR-DOC-18], [OAR-OPS-3]-[OAR-OPS-5]).

on_fire.description: Closed vocabulary of engine side-effects applied when the rule fires and is enforced. Conditions never mutate state ([OAR-DOC-19], [OAR-FIRE-1], [OAR-FACT-10]).

overrides.description: Rules this rule suppresses for an occurrence at which it fires. Declarative mutual exclusion, replacing hand-inlined negation of a sibling's condition ([OAR-DOC-20], [OAR-EVAL-13]-[OAR-EVAL-17]).

requires.description: What the rule needs from the host. Declaring it is what makes portability computable from the document alone ([OAR-DOC-21], [OAR-FACT-19], [OAR-FACT-20]).

profiles.description: Capability profile names the rule's facts come from.

facts.description: Individual fact or function names the rule needs, including host-tier names.

counter_scope.description: Names the declared string fact whose value keys this rule's counters. Absent means the counters are keyed by the rule and the session alone ([OAR-DOC-32], [OAR-FIRE-10]).

references.description: Interoperability taxonomy tags, for example owasp_llm or mitre_atlas. Never affects a decision ([OAR-DOC-25]).

status.description: The author's confidence in the rule. Never affects a decision; acting on it is the operator's job, via enforcement and the configuration document ([OAR-DOC-29]).

related.description: Rule lineage, so a retired identifier stays traceable to the rule that replaced it. Never affects a decision, and a target need not be loaded ([OAR-DOC-30]).

^x-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$.description: Implementation extension. An engine ignores one it does not recognise, and it never affects a decision ([OAR-DOC-26]).

allOf.$comment: [OAR-DOC-23] detector is present if and only if kind is detector.
[OAR-DOC-22] transform is present if and only if effect is transform.

factName.description: A fact or observation function name. A dotted name is a host-tier fact under [OAR-FACT-18].

ruleRef.description: A bare id, resolved in the referring rule's own namespace, or a qualified <namespace>/<id>.

onFireAction.description: increment_counter and reset_counter write the core fact fire_count; increment_breaker and reset_breaker write breaker_count; publish_event writes no fact ([OAR-FIRE-3]).

selector.description: Clauses are named by declared facts and match by set membership; clauses are conjunctive and an omitted clause is permissive. A clause naming a fact the engine does not declare is a load error, never a silent match ([OAR-SEL-1]-[OAR-SEL-8]).

transform.description: A content mutation. Transforms accumulate across the rules that fire at an occurrence and apply in evaluation order ([OAR-OPS-13]-[OAR-OPS-18]).

action.description: redact removes the target, substituting the engine's placeholder when no replacement is given; replace substitutes the given replacement; annotate attaches the replacement without removing the target.

target.description: Either the literal string content, meaning the whole content at this anchor, or the name of a declared list<map> fact whose members carry the spans to act on ([OAR-OPS-14]).

replacement.description: Required for replace and annotate; optional for redact.

detector.description: Present if and only if kind is detector ([OAR-DOC-23]).

ref.description: A registered detector. An engine rejects a reference it cannot resolve ([OAR-OPS-12]).

copy.description: Presentation text. A closed set of optional strings that MAY contain the bindings of Appendix C. No member may affect selection, evaluation, ordering, precedence, or the decision ([OAR-DOC-24], [OAR-COPY-6]).
